the c.34GT transversion is a marker for the diagnosis of MAP and that it can be used for prescreening of patients with adenomas.
the c.34 G>T KRAS mutation is a useful and promising prescreening test to guide genetic testing toward MUTYH in patients with familial adenomatous polyps.
we investigated the somatic mutation c.34G> T KRAS as a marker suggestive for the genetic condition MUTYH-associated colorectal cancer.

the development of new prescreening tests to identify individuals with an increased risk of developing colorectal cancer.
the development of a prescreening tool that could be applied to all colorectal cancer patients.
the somatic c34G>T KRas mutation as a marker of MUTYH associated polyposis (MUTYH/APC) and its potential for prescreening of patients with colorectal adenomas and cancers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the c.34 G>T KRAS mutation is a promising prescreening test in patients with polyposis, and that it is a useful test in patients with CRC.
the c.34GT mutation in KRAS is not a reliable test for the diagnosis of MAP.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the c.34 G>T KRAS mutation is an interesting marker for the diagnosis of MAP and should be included in the prescreening panel for polyposis patients.

the c.34 G→T transversion is an interesting and promising test for MUTYH-associated colorectal cancer and polyposis, with the potential to detect a significant number of patients with a germline MUTH gene mutation, even when they do not meet current genetic testing criteria.
the c.34GT KRAS transversion is a useful prescreening test to identify MUTYH mutation carriers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the c.34GT KRAS transversion can be used to identify MAP patients.
the KRAS transversion is a useful and promising tool to detect MAP patients and may be useful in CRC patients.
the somatic c.G34T mutation in the KRAS gene is a promising marker to identify patients with MAP, and that this mutation is also present in a subset of sporadic CRC patients.
